reviews: The gunplay and spray patterns still feel unmatched—landing a clean AK-47 one-tap on Mirage never stops being satisfying.
Economy management makes every round tense; deciding whether to force-buy or full-save after losing pistol round can swing the entire half.
Learning smoke lineups and pop-flashes on Inferno completely changed how our five-stack takes banana control.
Premier matchmaking is hit or miss—some matches are super close 13-11 nail-biters and others get ruined by spinbotters.
The sub-tick hit registration feels inconsistent compared to 128-tick FACEIT servers, especially when holding tight AWP angles.
Dust 2 and Nuke remain timeless map designs, though solo-queuing Nuke without team comms is basically a guaranteed loss.
Toxicity in voice chat is still rough if you whiff a 1v1 clutch, so muting teammates early saves your mental.
Watching the skins market turn into a stock exchange is wild, even if you never open a single case.
Movement and counter-strafing have a steep learning curve, but once it clicks no other tactical shooter feels as crisp.
Wingman 2v2 is underrated when you only have twenty minutes and want fast, intense rounds with a friend.
VAC needs serious work—high-elo Premier lobbies above 20k rating still run into blatant wallhackers way too often.
Audio cues for footsteps and bomb plants are super clear, letting you read rotations across the map with good headphones.
Pistol rounds are chaotic and fun, especially pulling off a clean USP-S headshot ace on pistol eco.
Bots being removed from competitive matches makes a teammate disconnecting feel like an instant loss.
Overtime rounds in competitive are pure adrenaline when both teams are low on utility and money.
My teammate screamed 'RUSH B' in three different languages and somehow we actually won the round.
Bought this game for free and somehow spent $200 on virtual knife pixels, send financial advice.
Specs: Ryzen 7 7800X3D, RTX 4070 Ti, 32GB DDR5. Getting 400+ FPS on 1280x960 stretched.
